# Understanding - haha - trying to Understanding

- Scenario - we will answer the questions with this sencario in mind
   - Subscription plan - cahche TTL is 1 hour
   - Current model set to Opus
   - Current context window is at 500k
   - Current cache status is warm with TTL ~ 59 minutes
- Sources
   - we refered to [How Claude Code uses prompt caching](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching) 
   - And an exepriement described int eh references 1 seciton below 
- Q1 - When i change models what happens and how are costs incurred 
   - when I call `model fable` nothing happens and actually no charges are incurred
   - but the next thign i trigger a message or a tool call or wahtever will now use Fable as the model and it will check if there is a cache of the context window
   - since i jsut changed model this model fable isntance does not have a cache so before this fable isntance can do anyhting it needs to write the context wiindow into cache thus incuring a input token usage cost by `cache write`
   - this cost of this inptu tokne usea by `cache write` is proportional to how big thecontext widnos is
- Q2 - Is the model switching cost  associated with Context Window size - Yes!
   - Answer in Q1 Answer. YES!
- Q3 - Q3 does swithcing mutiple tiemns a session re-incure hte input context cost - Yes!
   - based ont he docs and expriemnts; Yes
   - Every time we change mdoels the isntance of the model is new and a cache write needs to happeng (the cost of which is directly proportinoal to context window size)
- Q4 - Does model cohice effect the cost of callign `/compact` - Yes 
   - Yes it does but how much it costs dpeends on teh state of the sesssion (TTL state, context window, current model, new model)
   - Beacuse you ened to take into account the TTL stat and potnetial Cacche writes
   - Even then waht compact does is that that it takes the cached context window sumarmizes intoa  markdown or samll toducment and clear and just reads that
   - so the engine tht does the ocmapct yes is cost dpenidng ont he mode doing it
   - but often the main cost hsit he cold wreite of the cache of a cold session
- Q5 - what about cahce and idle sessions?
   - touched on in above answers but more detilas here
   - All sessions have  timer called TTL (Time To Live) - its a count down for time alive
   - For subscsirption absed sessions this is 60 mintues defualt; for API sessions it is 5 miuntes default
   - Any aciton freshes the timer
   - Once it runs down a session is considered cold and then the cache is deleted
   - this is bad ebuase the enxt time a actinois treigiere the session will need to rerwite the cache (cost proprotional to the size of the context window)



## Ref 1 - experiment: does `/model` send a request?

Full protocol and raw output in [Experiments](#experiments) below. Run in this session, on a Max subscription, 146k context, Opus 5.5 → Fable 5.1.

**Result: `/model` is free. The cost lands on the next message, as a full cache rewrite on the new model.**

| Entry | Model | Cache write | Cache read |
|---|---|---|---|
| `baseline` reply | opus-5-5 | 417 | 146,397 |
| `/model fable` | local command, no API call | - | - |
| `/usage` | local command, no API call | - | - |
| `check` reply | **fable-5-1** | **141,559** | **0** |

- The two slash commands are stored in the transcript as `local_command` entries with no token usage. `/usage` before and after the switch showed the same miss count and no Fable line.
- The first Fable reply wrote the whole 141k context to a 1-hour cache and read nothing. At API prices that's about **$2.80** for one message, against about $0.03 for the Opus reply just before it.
- Bonus finding: `/usage` reported the session's only other miss as "idle past the 1h TTL, 82.7k tokens re-cached". That is Q5 observed: an idle gap over an hour cost one full context rewrite.
- Bonus finding: the session cost line matched the price table to the cent (4.6m reads × $0.20 + 194k writes × $8 + 25.7k output × $20 ≈ $2.98 vs $2.99 shown), so 1-hour cache writes are billed at 2× input.
- Bonus finding: a switch also changes the system prompt. Claude Code tells the agent which model it is and rewrites the commit attribution line, so the prefix is not byte-identical across models.
